title: Per-polygon simplification causes slivers and dark triangles
evidence: deploy/migrations/116-area-vector-tiles.sql:41 `ST_AsMVTGeom(ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(ST_Transform(g.geometry, 3857), tile.tolerance), tile.bounds, 4096, 64, true)`: each polygon is simplified independently. Re-running that SQL in the local DB (scratchpad ov.sh) and intersecting the outputs: lsoa 9/256/169 (London+Essex): 633 features, 864 neighbour pairs overlapping >=1 unit², total overlap 19,650 unit², vs 3 unit² with quantisation only; union cover drops 16,749,023 -> 16,728,944 (≈20k unit² of gaps). lsoa 11/1023/680: 856 pairs, 24,091 overlap. lsoa 12/2046/1361: 218 pairs, 8,919. msoa 7/64/42: 1,771 pairs, 30,144. 0 invalid outputs, so the triangles are not caused by invalid geometry. The same tile with ST_CoverageSimplify(g3, tol) OVER () (scratchpad cov.sh): overlap 2 unit², 1 pair, cover 16,749,225 (no gaps), 31,933 points vs 23,257 now. PostGIS 3.6.4 / GEOS 3.14.1 already has ST_CoverageSimplify.
problem: Douglas–Peucker run on each ring separately drops a shared-edge vertex in polygon A but keeps it in neighbour B. The chord cuts a triangle either into B (painted twice: darker) or out of both (basemap shows through). This is exactly the 'they don't join, black triangles' symptom. TopoJSON/mapshaper simplify over a shared arc topology to avoid it, and tippecanoe keeps the nodes where shared borders meet (--no-simplification-of-shared-nodes, which replaced --detect-shared-borders).
proposal: Simplify the coverage, not each polygon. In the tile build, replace ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology with a per-zoom, precomputed coverage: for each zoom band, ST_CoverageSimplify(ST_Transform(geometry,3857), tol_z) OVER (PARTITION BY region or all England) into a derived table area_geometry_z(kind, z, id, geom). Then ST_AsMVTGeom without further simplification. Alternative: export once to GeoJSON/FlatGeobuf and run tippecanoe with --no-simplification-of-shared-nodes, or simplify once with mapshaper. Add a CI check (MAP-8).
deletes_code: none directly; makes the GeoJSON-path tolerances (MAP-5) unnecessary
verify_note: 116:41 uses ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology per polygon (each feature separately). I re-ran the tile SQL for lsoa 9/256/169 via docker exec ae-pgold psql and got 635 features, 864 pairs overlapping by at least 1 unit², 19,650 unit² of overlap against 3 unit² with quantisation only, and a union cover of 17,783,247 against 17,805,428 (about 22k unit² of gaps). The same tile with ST_CoverageSimplify(...) OVER () gave 2 unit² of overlap and a cover of 17,805,631, so no gaps. PostGIS is 3.6.4 and GEOS is 3.14 or later. One caveat: at the tile's own zoom the error is under a pixel (3/4096 of the tile width, about 0.375 px). The visible triangles need the overzoom in MAP-2. This is still the root mechanism.

title: z12 max zoom plus overzoom to z22 magnifies slivers
evidence: api/area_api/map_tiles.py:28 MAX_ZOOM = 12; the 116 header says 'the map overzooms 12 further in'. No maxZoom is set on the map (grep maxZoom in area-map.tsx shows only fitBounds 15), so MapLibre's default of 22 applies. Tolerance at z12 = 3/4096 of 9,784 m = 7.2 Mercator metres. That is 6 px at z16 (1.19 m/px for 512 px tiles) and 24 px at z18. The fill only fades at z>=12 when sales are on (lib/map-property-layers.ts:221 AREA_FADE_ZOOM = 12).
problem: At its own zoom the tolerance is 0.375 px, but the tiles are stretched 16–1000× past that. Every per-polygon simplification error becomes a visible wedge exactly where users zoom to inspect streets. geojson-vt (default maxZoom 14) and tippecanoe both treat the max zoom as near-lossless.
proposal: Make the max-zoom tiles lossless or near-lossless: tolerance about 0 at z12 (or build to z13/z14; LSOA z12 tiles are only 19 kB max, so there is room). Combined with MAP-1, any remaining error is the same on both sides of every edge.
deletes_code: none
verify_note: map_tiles.py:26 has MAX_ZOOM = 12, and the 116 header says the map overzooms past 12. The constructor at area-map.tsx:621-638 sets no maxZoom, and no maxZoom outside fitBounds/cameraForBounds was found, so MapLibre's default of 22 applies. The tolerance arithmetic holds: 7.2 m at z12, which is about 6 px at z16 with 512 px tiles. AREA_FADE_ZOOM = 12 is at map-property-layers.ts:221.

title: District layer comes from a different ONS product
evidence: deploy/tools/boundaries.py:19-35 takes LSOA from 'LSOA Dec 2021 BGC V5', MSOA from 'MSOA Dec 2021 BGC V3', and LAD from 'Local_Authority_Districts_May_2026_Boundaries_UK_BGC', a separate generalisation and year. SQL: symmetric difference between LAD and the union of its LSOAs is Camden 116,096 m², Epping Forest 293,419 m², Reigate 267,245 m²; Hausdorff of the boundaries is Camden 23 m, Epping 25 m, Thurrock 72 m. MSOA vs union of its LSOAs is 1–13 m², so those two nest. ST_CoverageInvalidEdges on 7 neighbouring LADs (Camden/Barnet/Enfield/Epping/Hertsmere/Haringey/Islington): 4 invalid. The LSOA coverage over the same area has 0.
problem: The 'borough' tiles, the selected-district outline (wider-area-outline) and zone shapes drawn over LSOA fills cross the LSOA edges by up to tens of metres. The LAD layer also doesn't tile seamlessly by itself, so the district choropleth shows its own slivers.
proposal: Build the parent levels from the base level: LAD (and region) = ST_CoverageUnion of their LSOAs (MSOA already nests). Keep the ONS LAD polygon only for metadata/QA. Run this check on every load: ST_CoverageInvalidEdges = 0 per level, and symdiff(parent, union(children)) = 0. Because area_geography is immutable (trigger area_geography_immutable), put the derived shapes in a new derived/generalised table rather than editing it.
deletes_code: LAD download branch in boundaries.py (~10 LOC)
verify_note: boundaries.py:19-35 takes LSOA from Dec 2021 BGC V5, MSOA from V3 and LAD from the May 2026 UK BGC. My SQL gave symdiff(LAD, union of its LSOAs via MSOA parent) of 116,096 m² for Camden and 293,419 m² for Epping Forest, with boundary Hausdorff distances of 23 m and 25 m in EPSG:27700. ST_CoverageInvalidEdges over the 7 named LADs returned 4 invalid edges, while the LSOA coverage over Camden/Barnet/Enfield/Epping/Hertsmere had 0 of 674. 'borough' is a tile kind (map_tiles.py:24), so the mismatch is drawn on the map.

title: 0.88 fill opacity and dark basemap expose every gap
evidence: web/src/lib/map-selection-paint.ts:9-12: OBSERVED_FILL_OPACITY 0.88, SELECTED 0.95, FALLBACK 0.8, SUPPRESSED 0.35. evidence: Kill switch CLOSE_KNIT_AREA_TILES=off (api/area_api/map_tiles.py:57). The London coverage and demo modes also load GeoJSON (web/src/lib/area-tiles.ts:7-9; map-coverage.ts:104-105). Measured on 182 MSOAs in 6 north-London boroughs (~193 km²): 0.003° gives 9.3 km² of overlap (234 pairs >1,000 m²) and 21.9 km² of net area lost; 0.001° gives 2.96 km² of overlap. proposal: Make vector tiles the only path. Serve demo/fixture boundaries as a small static .pmtiles/.mbtiles built by the same tool. Move home-mini-map-canvas.tsx (the remaining polyline user) onto the same tile source. Delete the polyline codec, DETAIL tolerances, source-diff, the GeoJSON fill branches in area-map.tsx, and the 'region' detail kept for old clients. deletes_code: ~500-800 LOC (geometry_codec.py 89, geometry-codec.ts 54, area-source-diff.ts 52, most of real-geometry.ts 221, GeoJSON branches of area-map.tsx, 3 test files)

title: Tiles built in Postgres and served through two app hops
evidence: Tiles are stored as bytea in area_tile (local: 16,687 tiles, 38.6 MB, built 2026-10-25). Built by area_tile_mvt + build_area_tiles() plpgsql (116:30-99) and deploy/tools/build_area_tiles.sql. Served by FastAPI api/area_api/app.py:1116 get_area_tile (active-release lookup + tile query per request) behind a Next.js proxy, web/src/app/api/v1/tiles/areas/[release]/[kind]/[z]/[x]/[y]/route.ts; 9 tile proxy routes in total under app/api/v1/tiles. The release id is a hash of area ids only (116:24-28), so a geometry/simplification change can't produce a new release without new ids. Doc drift: the 116 header says 'Built by deploy/tools/build_area_tiles.sh', but the file is .sql.
problem: Boundaries are static per release, the textbook case for pre-built static tiles. Building them in a migration-defined SQL function, keeping them in the OLTP database and streaming them through Python and Node adds latency, connection load and code. Also, the release key can't express 'same areas, better geometry', which is the exact change MAP-1/2/3 needs.
proposal: Pipeline: ETL loads ONS 2021 LSOA BGC, derives MSOA/LAD/region by coverage union (MAP-3), exports per-zoom coverage-simplified layers, or runs tippecanoe -Z5 -z13 with named layers msoa/lsoa/lad and --no-simplification-of-shared-nodes, into one areas-<hash>.pmtiles (hash of the file contents). Serve it from nginx/CDN as an immutable file (MapLibre pmtiles protocol, or Martin if a server is wanted). Delete area_tile, area_tile_build, build_area_tiles(), area_tile_mvt and the FastAPI and Next.js area-tile routes.
deletes_code: ~250 LOC (116 functions/tables, build_area_tiles.sql, map_tiles.py route parts, Next area tile route) + 38 MB of bytea in Postgres
verify_note: area_tile_build shows release a1-632ef58648dc with 16,687 tiles and 38,614,175 bytes, built 2026-10-25. The release is md5 of area ids only (116:27). The header says build_area_tiles.sh, but only deploy/tools/build_area_tiles.sql exists. There are 9 route.ts files under app/api/v1/tiles. Small correction: get_area_tile is at app.py:1121, not 1116.

evidence: The geometry is one coherent England coverage: ST_CoverageInvalidEdges over 674 LSOAs spanning Camden/Barnet/Enfield (London) and Epping Forest/Hertsmere (non-London) = 0 invalid; LSOA overlap in each LAD = 0 m². CLOSE_KNIT_ENGLAND (per FLAGS.md it must stay a flag) only limits which areas get values or are panned to (maxBounds and value packs), not which geometry pipeline runs. title: Region is a side table, not part of the hierarchy
evidence: DB: `select enum_range(null::geography_kind)` -> {lsoa,msoa,borough}; no region or country kind. deploy/migrations/103-england-geography.sql:27 lad_region (296 rows inlined as INSERTs) and :334 area_region(area_id, region_code, region_name), filled by an AFTER INSERT trigger fill_area_region (:342) plus refresh_area_region() (:368). The region list is copied in api/area_api/coverage.py:17 REGIONS, api/area_api/regions.py, web/src/lib/scope-name.ts:20, pipelines/area-analytics-ingest/area_analytics/england_lads.json, deploy/tools/etl_kids.py:46 and migration 103. API: 67 refs to lad_region/area_region/area_rank_region, and 12 SQL joins to area_region.
problem: London was the implicit root, and England was added through a lookup table next to area_geography. Regions and England have no id, no geometry and no page entity, so every consumer re-derives them: SQL joins, Python dicts cached for 10 minutes (regions.py REGIONS_TTL_SECONDS) and hard-coded TS arrays. The trigger only fires on INSERT, so a changed LAD-to-region mapping needs a manual refresh call.
proposal: Make the hierarchy first-class. Add 'region' and 'country' to geography_kind and insert 9 region rows plus 1 England row, with geometry from dissolving the LADs, or better from ONS region boundaries. Set parent_id LAD->region->country. Add denormalised columns lad_id, region_id and country_id to area_geography, populated once per geography release. Then drop area_region, lad_region, coverage.REGIONS and scope-name.ts constants; the region list comes from `SELECT ... WHERE kind='region'` and the API serves it to web via /map/coverage. Safe steps: (1) add the kinds and rows, with backfill and unchanged ids; (2) add the columns plus a view `area_region` that keeps old readers working; (3) switch readers module by module; (4) drop the side tables.
deletes_code: ~300 LOC (lad_region INSERT block, fill_area_region trigger, refresh_area_region, regions.py cache, 4 hard-coded region lists)

The region list is copied in coverage.py:17-27 REGIONS, web/src/lib/scope-name.ts:18 and pipelines/.../england_lads.json. title: London-named rank fields hold region ranks; England column is dead
evidence: DB: metric_value columns include london_percentile and england_percentile. `select count(*) filter (where england_percentile is null), count(*) from metric_value` -> 24915025 | 24915025 (100% NULL). The header of migration 103 (lines 1-6) says the region percentile is stored in london_percentile and 'column names stay for compatibility'. England ranks are computed at request time in Python instead: api/area_api/evidence.py:1966-1978 (_england_ranks -> map_chunks.england_ranks, overwriting the null column per row). contracts/openapi.yaml:2801 `londonPercentile ... description: "Percentile within the area's region (rankScope)"`. Usage counts: london_percentile api=58 sql=75; londonPercentile api=63 web=92 contracts=32; area_london_rank sql=34 (and that table holds only 4 rank_ids: best-primary, station-walk, quiet, park-distance).
problem: The public contract and the schema lie about meaning. A London percentile and a Leeds percentile share one field with different scopes, so a separate rankScope field had to be bolted on to explain it. The England-wide rank exists in two forms: a column that is always null, and a runtime computation in the API process that has to be warmed. Every new consumer (MCP, extension, pages) must know the trick.
proposal: Introduce scope-generic ranks. Add metric_value.region_percentile and country_percentile, both computed in SQL at release build by one function rank_metric(metric_id, period) with PARTITION BY region_id and PARTITION BY country_id. The alternative is a narrow metric_rank(geography_id, metric_id, period, scope_id, percentile) table. Rename area_london_rank to area_rank. In the API contract, add regionPercentile and englandPercentile (filled), and keep londonPercentile as a deprecated alias for one version for the MCP and extension. Then delete _england_ranks, map_chunks.england_ranks and its cache.
deletes_code: ~150 LOC runtime ranking (evidence._england_ranks, map_chunks.england_ranks, ENGLAND_RANK_SQL) plus the null column

title: Seam patched at request time: regex rewording and post-query filters
evidence: api/area_api/regions.py:142 `_LONDON_WORDS = re.compile(r"(?<=% of )London\b|(?<=most of )London\b|\bLondon(?=['’]s\b)")`; regional_words() walks the whole payload and substitutes the region name. It is applied to every area route in api/area_api/app.py:1500-1508 (_scoped). regions.region_view (:165) filters cached all-England dicts by key prefix 'uk:'. regions.filter_rows (:177) filters rows in Python. Scope helpers are called 47 times (repository 12, evidence 11, custom_criteria 9, personal_places 8, area_pages 8 ...). feature_flags.england()/coverage.england() appears in 24 API branches. api/area_api/*.py has 752 'london' mentions.
problem: The copy is written for London, then rewritten by regex after the fact. That breaks on new phrasings ('London average', 'across London') and silently misleads. Region scoping is done after querying, so queries read all of England and Python throws rows away; correctness depends on every new endpoint remembering to wrap. This is the 'tape and sticks' the owner feels.
proposal: (1) Generate copy from a template with an explicit scope name (`f"{pct}% of {scope.name}"`) at the source modules, then delete regional_words. (2) Push scope into SQL: once region_id is a column on area_geography (A1), every query takes `region_id = ANY(%(scope)s)` from one request-scoped Scope object, built once in a FastAPI dependency from the CLOSE_KNIT_ENGLAND flag and the requested regions. Delete region_view, filter_rows and keeper. (3) Add a test that fails if any payload string contains 'London' for a non-London area.
deletes_code: ~120 LOC in regions.py + ~47 call-site wrappers
verify_note: Right: _LONDON_WORDS regex at regions.py:144, regional_words at :147, applied in app.py:1508 inside _scoped (22 uses). region_view and filter_rows do filter in Python (14 call sites, e.g. repository.py:281,367; personal_places.py:200; borough_standouts.py:192). About 50 regions.* calls outside regions.py. Overstated: scope already reaches SQL in 4 places via scope_clause. The regex is deliberately narrow, so the 'silently misleads' risk is real but limited to copy. The request-time patching is real debt, but it is not as severe as the data-model issues.

title: Same layer, different data and method on each side
evidence: SQL (local ae-pgold): metrics present only for London areas = 19 (crime, nature-score, wildlife-*, hmo-per-1000, short-lets-per-1000, pipeline-homes-per-1000, stock-value-per-square-metre, future-station-distance); only for non-London = 7 (noise, flood-risk, typical-price, typical-price-{flat,terraced,semi,detached}); both = 637. Per region: flood-risk lon_rows=0 eng_rows=28761; noise 0/28761; typical-price 0/28761; crime 72348/0. Yet area_flood has London rows (12058) and so does area_noise: London's flood and noise sit in bespoke tables, not metric rows. deploy/tools/etl_england_environment_bundle.py:4-13 says it loads 'for every non-London area' and that 'London's flood, noise and air rows stay as they are'. The client hard-codes coverage in web/src/lib/map-topics.ts:361 LAYER_COVERAGE (air-no2, short-lets, hmo, canopy ...), and metric_definition has no coverage column (id,carrier,unit,direction,definition,source_release_id). Caveat: local England crime is not loaded (crime 0 non-London rows) while report.md says prod has it, so local and prod differ.
problem: A metric id is not one dataset: for London it comes from the old ETL, method and table, and for the rest of England from a new bundle. Values meet at the M25 with different methods (e.g. Defra noise in London vs Round 4 outside). Coverage is not data but a TS constant that drifts from the release. Re-run the national flood, noise and typical-price loaders for London too and publish London's flood-risk and noise as metric_value rows; delete the London-only code paths once values are reconciled. Keep source-limited layers (TfL, GLA, HMO) but record coverage in the data: add metric_definition.coverage_scope_id, or compute it as the regions present in metric_value at release build, and expose it in /metrics. Delete LAYER_COVERAGE in web. Add a release gate that fails when a metric's region coverage changes unexpectedly between releases.
deletes_code: LAYER_COVERAGE + isLondonOnly (~30 LOC web); later the London-only branches of the flood/noise loaders
verify_note: Reproduced the counts: 19 metrics only in London, 7 only outside London, 637 in both. flood-risk, noise and typical-price have 0 London and 28,761 non-London rows; crime has 72,348 London and 0 non-London. area_flood has 12,058 London rows. LAYER_COVERAGE (map-topics.ts:361) is hard-coded and metric_definition has no coverage column. The two sides do use different methods: england_noise.py:3 says London keeps its per-home etl_noise build while the rest of England uses the Defra layer. The env bundle header confirms that London rows 'stay as they are'. Not supported: the claim that London's flood and noise exist only in bespoke tables. rebuild_flood_risk (103:~1503) deletes and rebuilds flood-risk for every LSOA from dwelling_flood, and etl_noise_layer.py writes a London noise layer, so missing London metric rows look like a local-load artefact, not the design. title: Boundaries simplified per polygon, so neighbours overlap and gap
evidence: deploy/migrations/116-area-vector-tiles.sql:41 `ST_AsMVTGeom(ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(ST_Transform(g.geometry, 3857), tile.tolerance) ...)` runs per feature. The GeoJSON path does the same at api/area_api/evidence.py:354,391 and brief.py:60. Measured on London MSOAs at z7 tolerance (229 m, as 116 computes for z7): `ST_Overlaps` neighbour pairs after simplification = 1921, overlap ~86 km² in EPSG:3857 (raw = 0). Union area 4055 -> 3931, i.e. ~3% of the area becomes gaps. PostGIS 3.6.4 / GEOS 3.14 are installed, so ST_CoverageSimplify is available.
problem: Simplifying each polygon independently moves shared edges differently for each neighbour. That produces exactly the overlaps, slivers and dark 'triangles' (double-painted semi-transparent fills and outline AA) the owner sees when zooming. No tile LOD trick fixes it; it is the generalisation step.
proposal: Generalise as a coverage, once per geography release: for each kind and zoom band, `ST_CoverageSimplify(geom, tol) OVER (PARTITION BY kind)` (or mapshaper/tippecanoe with shared arcs), stored in area_geometry_generalised(kind, zband, id, geom). Build tiles from that with no per-feature simplify. Derive MSOA, LAD and region shapes by dissolving the generalised LSOAs so levels nest exactly. Add a test asserting zero ST_Overlaps between neighbours per zoom band.
deletes_code: per-request simplify SQL in evidence.py/brief.py once the GeoJSON path is gone
verify_note: 116:37 sets tolerance = tile width*3/4096 (229 m at z7) and 116:41 applies ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology to each feature; evidence.py:352,390 and brief.py:60 do the same. Re-ran on London MSOAs at 229.3 m: 1,923 overlapping neighbour pairs (raw 0), 87 km² of overlap, union area 4,055 -> 3,931 km². Checked the gaps separately from the outer edge: 119 km² of the raw union lying more than 500 m inside the outer boundary is uncovered after simplification, so interior gaps are real. ST_CoverageSimplify exists (PostGIS 3.6.4, GEOS 3.14.1). That this causes the 'black triangles' is plausible but was not observed visually.

title: Migrations: no ledger, fresh DB skips England, copy-paste redefinitions
evidence: 105 files numbered 001-118 (gaps 104,106,108,111,114). No schema_migrations-style table in DB. deploy/docker-compose.yml:39-134 mounts 93 of 105 migrations into initdb; missing: 068 070 072 090 103 107 109 110 112 113 115 116, so a fresh local DB has no area_region and no area_tile_mvt, i.e. a London-only schema. deploy/schema.sql has 21 CREATE TABLE vs 142 tables in DB. preflight.sh:65-79 hand-checks individual indexes ('apply 115/117/118'). 126 CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION across files for only 72 distinct functions (property_tile x8, rebuild_area_people/noise/stock_values/load_sales x4). 103-england-geography.sql is 1,774 lines, mostly verbatim copies of earlier rebuild_* functions with only PARTITION BY changed (its header lines 14-22).

title: Per-feature simplification causes gaps/overlaps
evidence: deploy/migrations/116-area-vector-tiles.sql:41 `ST_AsMVTGeom(ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(ST_Transform(g.geometry, 3857), tile.tolerance)...` (each area simplified on its own); same pattern for the GeoJSON path at api/area_api/evidence.py:354,391 and repository.py:549. SQL on ae-pgold, 70 MSOAs in E09000033/E09000020/E09000013 with the tile tolerance per zoom: z5 tol 917 m -> overlap 642.7 ha, net gap 3,491 ha; z7 tol 229 m -> 380.1 ha overlap / 753.6 ha gap; z9 -> 57.3 / 91.6 ha. Add a SQL test that asserts sum(area) - area(union) stays near zero for one LAD per band.

Draw borders as one line layer from the same tiles, a thin --ink at low alpha, instead of relying on fill-antialias seams. Draw the selected outline from the same tile features with a feature-state line, not a separate GeoJSON. Add a DB check that fails the build if the sum of pairwise intersection area in any sample tile is above 0.

title: Zoom fade snaps on zoomend
